title: The ark is sent on to Ekron — the Greek names Ascalon (Askelon)
summary: The KJV says the Philistines sent the ark to Ekron (5:10) and that the five lords returned to Ekron (6:16). The Hebrew prints עֶקְרוֹן in both verses. Brenton’s Greek prints Ἀσκάλωνα (Ascalon) in both.
text: KJV 1 Samuel 5:10: “Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 5:10: Καὶ ἐξαποστέλλουσι τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα· καὶ ἐγενήθη ὡς εἰσῆλθε κιβωτὸς Θεοῦ εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα, καὶ ἐβόησαν οἱ Ἀσκαλωνῖται, λέγοντες, τί ἀπεστρέψατε τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς ἡμᾶς θανατῶσαι ἡμᾶς καὶ τὸν λαὸν ἡμῶν; [and they send away the ark of God to Ascalon; and when the ark of God came into Ascalon, the Ascalonites cried out]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 6:16: Καὶ οἱ πέντε σατράπαι τῶν ἀλλοφύλων ἑώρων, καὶ ἀνέστρεψαν εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ. [and the five satraps of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon on that day]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 6:16: “And the five lords of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon in that day.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA05.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/5/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA05.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA05.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA06.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA06.htm.
reasoning: In both verses the Hebrew reads Ekron and the Greek reads Ascalon, so the Greek tradition sends the ark, and the lords, to a different Philistine city. In the Greek the same chapter’s list of golden emerods (6:17) names both Ascalon and Accaron (Ekron), so a reader of the Greek has Ascalon as the third city of the ark’s journey and Accaron as the last city in the list.

title: “The judge shall judge him” — the Greek has “they shall pray for him to the Lord”
summary: The KJV has Eli say, “If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him”. The Hebrew is וּפִלְלוֹ אֱלֹהִים. Brenton’s Greek reads καὶ προσεύξονται ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πρὸς Κύριον, “and they shall pray for him to the Lord”.

[if a man sins against a man, they shall pray for him to the Lord; and if he sins against the Lord, who shall pray for him?]. title: Why the men of Bethshemesh were smitten — the Greek adds “the sons of Jechonias were not pleased”
summary: The KJV says the Lord smote the men of Bethshemesh “because they had looked into the ark of the Lord”. The Hebrew says כִּי רָאוּ בַּאֲרוֹן יְהוָה, “because they saw into the ark of the LORD”. Brenton’s Greek opens with a different clause: οὐκ ἠσμένισαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰεχονίου ἐν τοῖς ἀνδράσι Βαιθσαμύς, “the sons of Jechonias were not pleased with the men of Bethshemesh”, and then adds “because they saw the ark of the Lord”.
text: KJV 1 Samuel 6:19: “And he smote the men of Bethshemesh, because they had looked into the ark of the Lord, even he smote of the people fifty thousand and threescore and ten men: and the people lamented, because the Lord had smitten many of the people with a great slaughter.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 6:19: וַיַּ֞ךְ בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י רָאוּ֙ בַּאֲרֹ֣ון יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֤ךְ בָּעָם֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽתְאַבְּל֣וּ הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּעָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדֹולָֽה ׃ [and he struck among the men of Bethshemesh because they saw into the ark of the LORD, and he struck among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men]. A reader of the Greek has a named family in the story whom the Hebrew does not name. The number is the same in both: seventy men and fifty thousand men.

title: Saul sleeps “in the trench” — the Greek has him sleeping “in a chariot”
summary: The KJV says Saul “lay in the trench” (26:5) and “within the trench” (26:7). The Hebrew word is בַּמַּעְגָּל in both verses. Brenton’s Greek prints ἐν λαμπήνῃ, which Brenton’s English renders “in a chariot” (a covered carriage or wagon).
text: KJV 1 Samuel 26:5: “And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had pitched: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay in the trench, and the people pitched round about him.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 26:5: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיָּבֹא֮ אֶֽל־הַמָּקֹום֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָנָה־שָׁ֣ם שָׁאוּל֒ וַיַּ֣רְא דָּוִ֗ד אֶת־הַמָּקֹום֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָֽׁכַב־שָׁ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וְאַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־נֵ֖ר שַׂר־צְבָאֹ֑ו וְשָׁאוּל֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב בַּמַּעְגָּ֔ל וְהָעָ֖ם חֹנִ֥ים [סְבִיבֹתֹו כ] (סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃ ק) [and Saul was lying in the encampment [or: wagon-circle], and the people were camped around him]. title: “The king of Israel is come out to seek a flea” — the Greek has “to seek my life”
summary: The KJV has David say the king of Israel “is come out to seek a flea”. The Hebrew is לְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־פַּרְעֹשׁ אֶחָד, “to seek one flea”. Brenton’s Greek reads ζητεῖν ψυχήν μου, “to seek my life”.
text: KJV 1 Samuel 26:20: “Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 26:20: וְעַתָּ֗ה אַל־יִפֹּ֤ל דָּֽמִי֙ אַ֔רְצָה מִנֶּ֖גֶד פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָצָ֞א מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֣שׁ אֶחָ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִרְדֹּ֥ף הַקֹּרֵ֖א בֶּהָרִֽים׃ [for the king of Israel has come out to seek one flea, as one pursues the partridge on the mountains]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 26:20: Καὶ νῦν μὴ πέσοι τὸ αἷμά μου ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἐξεναντίας προσώπου Κυρίου, ὅτι ἐξελήλυθεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ ζητεῖν ψυχήν μου, καθὼς καταδιώκει ὁ νυκτικόραξ ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι. [for the king of Israel has come out to seek my life, as the night-raven pursues in the mountains]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 26:20: “And now let not my blood fall to the ground before ††Gr. the face of the Lord.the Lord, for the king of Israel has come forth to seek thy life, as the night hawk pursues its prey in the mountains.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA26.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/26/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA26.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA26.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew compares the pursuit to hunting one flea, and the same word appears in 24:14. The Greek has David’s life as the object of the search and does not print “flea” here.
